ai.title: Handle leaked SEARCH/REPLACE blocks in processFileBlock
ai.summary: processFileBlock now detects leaked SEARCH/REPLACE markers in updatedContent and triggers applyRemainingChanges with normalizedNewContent instead of diffBlocksThatDidntMatch. applyRemainingChanges signature updated to accept changes string and filePath. Covers backend/src/process-file-block.ts.

eli5.text: The system that applies text edits to files now catches a leak of leftover edit commands. If a completed edit still contains the special markers that label a search-and-replace block, the system stops, logs the problem, and hands the file plus the unapplied changes to a fresh rewrite pass instead of the usual leftover-diff pass. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it prevents edits from being silently dropped or mangled when a previous edit leaves stray replacement commands in its wake. The change is internal and already live.

ai.title: Refine terminal command detection and skip list
ai.summary: Removes 'kill' and adds 'do' to SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS in common/src/constants.ts. Increases max word count for CLI command recognition from 4 to 5 in npm-app/src/cli.ts. Expands command-not-found detection in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts to catch /bin/sh errors, fatal:, and error: prefixes.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command, it now lets slightly longer commands through (up to five words instead of four) and better recognizes when the system tells it a command wasn't found, including errors from the standard shell and common error prefixes. At the same time, it stops automatically skipping over the words 'do' while still skipping 'kill', so short requests that happen to contain those words are handled more predictably. If you looked, you'd notice the assistant reacts more consistently to quick 'run' style prompts instead of misclassifying them or missing the error.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.111
ai.summary: Bump codebuff version to 1.0.111. Updates `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The software's version number was simply updated to 1.0.111, which is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping step to mark the latest batch of internal fixes and improvements. This update packages together a collection of smaller adjustments made over the past few days, including tweaks to how the assistant handles certain text formatting, improvements to error handling on specific pages, and refinements to automated checks. Nothing about the core features changes for end users, and you wouldn't notice anything different unless you were reviewing these specific edge-case behaviors.

ai.title: Usage-based pricing migration
ai.summary: Added DB migration 0007_equal_warlock.sql enforcing cascade deletes on `message` foreign keys to `user` and `fingerprint`. Updated `schema.ts` to reflect `onDelete: 'cascade'`. Stripe checkout session removed hardcoded `quantity: 1` to support usage-based pricing. Pricing page layout adjusted for cancellation link.

eli5.text: When you delete your account or request your data be removed, the application now automatically deletes the stored conversation records tied to you instead of leaving them behind. The payment system also stopped forcing a fixed quantity on checkout so it can switch to usage-based billing, and the pricing page was tweaked so a line break keeps the cancellation link readable. These changes are part of moving to usage-based pricing and are live as of the November 2024 migration.

ai.title: Add STRIPEOVERAGEPRICEID to checkout session
ai.summary: Stripe checkout session now includes a second line item for overage usage alongside the subscription price. Requires new `STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID` environment variable in `web/src/env.mjs`. Subscription line item explicitly sets `quantity: 1`.

eli5.text: When you or a subscriber starts the payment flow for the service, they will now see a second line on the checkout screen showing an additional item for extra usage. The system now reads a new pricing identifier from its configuration to know the price of that usage item. This affects people signing up or changing plans through the payment screen, who will see one more row in their cart than before.

ai.title: Add dedicated test and config file retrieval prompt
ai.summary: Introduced `generateTestAndConfigFilesPrompt` in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` to fetch test and config files separately from main logic files. Updated system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to mandate explicit verification steps using concatenated commands (e.g., `npm run lint && npm run test`) after edits.

eli5.text: The assistant now asks for test and configuration files in a separate step from other code files, so it can focus on those types more precisely. After making edits, it is now instructed to run verification commands like lint and test checks chained together, and skip those checks only for tiny, confident changes. You would notice this when the assistant finishes a task by running these combined check commands, or when it retrieves test files in their own dedicated pass instead of bundled with main code.

ai.title: Add Python defaults to file ignore list
ai.summary: Expanded `DEFAULT_IGNORED_FILES` in `common/src/constants.ts` to include Python-specific artifacts (`__pycache__`, `*.egg-info/`, `*.pyc`) and virtual environment directories (`venv`, `virtualenv`, `env`, `.venv`, `.virtualenv`, `ENV`). `common/src/project-file-tree.ts` now iterates over this constant to populate the `ignore` instance, replacing hardcoded additions. This prevents Freebuff from indexing irrelevant Python build and cache files.

eli5.text: The assistant can now skip over Python cache and virtual environment folders automatically when looking through your project files, so it won't accidentally list or read build artifacts like __pycache__ or.venv contents. If you browse the file list it builds, those folders and files such as *.pyc and *.egg-info will be hidden from view. This applies to every supported project type today.

ai.title: Bump codebuff to 1.0.112
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.112 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant now tracks your usage and bills you for any extra you use beyond your plan, automatically charging your card for the difference. When you check out, the billing screen shows a second line item with both your regular subscription and the pay-as-you-go amount for overage, so you see what you're being charged for. This is available to anyone on a usage-based subscription plan.
